risks.title: Persistent Inflationary Pressures
risks.summary: Inflation remains elevated above the Federal Reserve's 2% target, driven by supply shocks in sectors like energy and AI-related capital expenditures. While some moderation is expected, sticky inflation poses a risk to economic stability and monetary policy effectiveness.
risks.watch_for: June and July CPI and PCE data, Federal Reserve statements on inflation outlook.
sources: Guggenheim Investments (July 2026 Economic Outlook and Key Themes, July 20)
Stanford SIEPR (US Economy 2026: What to Watch, July 2026)

risks.title: Geopolitical Instability and Energy Price Volatility
risks.summary: Escalating geopolitical tensions, particularly the conflict in the Middle East and its impact on the Strait of Hormuz, are driving oil price volatility. This directly fuels inflation and creates uncertainty, complicating monetary policy decisions.
risks.watch_for: Developments in the Middle East conflict, Strait of Hormuz shipping status, oil price movements.
sources: Guggenheim Investments (Strong Earnings Outweighed by Worries Around Higher Oil and Interest Rates, July 27, 2026)
KPMG International (The butterfly effect: Geopolitical shocks, policy uncertainty & the economic outlook, March 10, 2026)

risks.title: Elevated US National Debt and Shrinking Fiscal Space
risks.summary: US national debt has surpassed the size of the economy, limiting the government's ability to borrow and respond to future shocks. High debt service costs and increased spending on rearmament and aging populations exacerbate this issue.
risks.watch_for: CBO's updated debt projections, Congressional budget debates.
sources: Stanford SIEPR (US Economy 2026: What to Watch, July 2026)
Congressional Budget Office (Budget and Economic Outlook: 2026 to 2036, February 11, 2026)
KPMG International (The butterfly effect: Geopolitical shocks, policy uncertainty & the economic outlook, March 10, 2026)

risks.title: AI Investment Boom and Productivity Dividend Uncertainty
risks.summary: Robust investment in Artificial Intelligence is a key driver of growth, but the full productivity dividend remains a promise. The costs of AI (chips, power, capital) are immediate, while the benefits may take time to materialize, creating potential for uneven economic impact.
risks.watch_for: Corporate AI capital spending announcements, productivity growth data.
sources: Guggenheim Investments (July 2026 Economic Outlook and Key Themes, July 20)
Stanford SIEPR (US Economy 2026: What to Watch, July 2026)
KPMG International (Spring thaw, summer heat: Biannual economic outlook, June 10, 2026)
Stanford SIEPR (2026 SIEPR Economic Summit, July 2026)

risks.title: Labor Market Resilience Amidst Shifting Dynamics
risks.summary: The labor market shows resilience with stabilizing unemployment, but job growth has slowed. Concerns exist about AI's potential impact on hiring and the risk of stagflation if unemployment rises while inflation remains high.
risks.watch_for: Monthly jobs reports (payrolls, unemployment rate, wage growth), AI's impact on hiring.
sources: Guggenheim Investments (July 2026 Economic Outlook and Key Themes, July 20)
Stanford SIEPR (US Economy 2026: What to Watch, July 2026)
NCCI (State of The Economy: What We're Watching July 2026, July 23, 2026)

risks.title: Monetary Policy Uncertainty and Fed's Hawkish Stance
risks.summary: The Federal Reserve, under new leadership, faces a challenging balancing act between controlling inflation and supporting employment. The absence of forward guidance and potential for further rate hikes create policy uncertainty.
risks.watch_for: FOMC statements, Federal Reserve Chair's speeches, market expectations for rate hikes.
sources: Stanford SIEPR (US Economy 2026: What to Watch, July 2026)
Kiplinger (Will the Federal Reserve raise interest rates? Here is what experts predict for July's meeting., July 27, 2026)
Lockhart Sees Fed Steady in July, at Least 50 Bps in Rate Hikes on the Way (July 28, 2026)

risks.title: Global Fragmentation and Trade Tensions
risks.summary: Fragmented global trade and ongoing tariff regimes create headwinds for economic growth. Supply chain disruptions and protectionist policies can lead to higher costs and reduced efficiency.
risks.watch_for: New tariff announcements, trade balance data, geopolitical developments impacting trade routes.
sources: KPMG International (Spring thaw, summer heat: Biannual economic outlook, June 10, 2026)
KPMG International (The butterfly effect: Geopolitical shocks, policy uncertainty & the economic outlook, March 10, 2026)

risks.title: Housing Market Affordability and Stability
risks.summary: Housing affordability remains a concern for consumers, and the housing market is described as being in a state of 'suspended animation.' This could dampen consumer spending and broader economic activity.
risks.watch_for: Housing starts, home sales data, mortgage rates.
sources: Stanford SIEPR (US Economy 2026: What to Watch, July 2026)

consensus_note: There is a strong consensus across institutions regarding persistent inflation and geopolitical risks stemming from the Middle East conflict as key concerns for the US and global economy in 2026. While AI investment is seen as a growth driver, its productivity benefits are viewed with some uncertainty. Divergence exists in the precise outlook for interest rates, with some anticipating holds and others expecting hikes later in the year, reflecting the Federal Reserve's challenging policy path.
